extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for or managing KAKENHI (Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research) in Japan
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing, submitting, reviewing, receiving, spending, and reporting Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research (KAKENHI) applications and funded projects in Japan (FY2022 edition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and nature of KAKENHI funding
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI is the only competitive research funding program aimed at all scientific research based on the free ideas of researchers across humanities, social sciences and natural sciences; it supports creative and pioneering research by individuals or small groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use KAKENHI to support scientific research originating from the applicant's own creative ideas (basic to applied). Choose the research category appropriate to content and scale (e.g., Specially Promoted Research, Transformative Research Areas, Scientific Research S/A/B/C, Challenging Research, Early-Career, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to apply (institutional affiliation and researcher status)
rubrics_metrics.description: At application time, the applicant must belong to a designated research institution and be recognized by that institution as a researcher who (a) has a job assignment including research activity, (b) is actually engaged in research activity (not only assisting roles), and (c) is not a graduate student or other student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be registered in e-Rad as eligible to apply. Some institution-specific conditions may apply—verify with your research institution. Being paid/unpaid or part-time/full-time is irrelevant for (a); concurrently holding student status while having a research-position job is allowed only if research-position job meets requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility due to prior penalties or misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who are categorized as ineligible for grant acquisition in the fiscal year (as a penalty for improper grant spending, fraudulent acquisition, or research misconduct using KAKENHI or other competitive funds) cannot apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm status before applying. Some research categories have different eligibility rules (e.g., Encouragement of Scientists, Research Activity Start-up).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural rules and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must follow the Application Procedures for Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research; the format of application documents may not be changed; corrections and resubmissions are not accepted after submission via the Electronic Application System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete three pre-application matters: (1) ascertain eligibility, (2) confirm researcher information registered via your research institution in e-Rad, (3) obtain an e-Rad ID/password from your research institution. Avoid errors/omissions in application fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on multiple applications and duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying for multiple research projects, applicants must eliminate unreasonable duplications and excessive concentration and avoid violations of restrictions on parallel submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check category-specific restrictions and structure proposals to avoid overlapping aims or budget double-dipping across proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-Investigator and Research Collaborator rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding a Co-Investigator, obtain consent of the prospective Co-Investigator and his/her research institution. Definitions: Principal Investigator (PI) - full responsibility; Co-Investigator - shares funds and responsibility; Research Collaborator - provides cooperation but is not a funded project member and has no discretion over KAKENHI funds. Non-eligible applicants may participate as Research Collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional approvals and consents before listing Co-Investigators. Note that the 'Collaborating Researcher' category was abolished (integrated into Research Collaborator).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement of proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI provides financial support for creative and pioneering research conducted by individual researchers; the contents of the research proposal must be originally planned by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare proposals that clearly demonstrate the applicant's original ideas, novelty, and creative contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of other funding (domestic and foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must declare any foreign research funds and, in future applications, all domestic and foreign competitive research funds as well as any research funding (including private subsidies, contract research, and joint research) in the Research Proposal Document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From FY2021, explicitly enter all external funds in 'The Status of Application and Acquisition of Research Grants' column. Be transparent to comply with Integrated Innovation Strategy and review requirements; see Supplement to Application Procedures for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are selected by peer review conducted by prominent researchers in each academic field; JSPS uses a reviewer candidate database (approx. 141,000 persons) and more than 8,000 researchers participate in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer names are disclosed on the KAKENHI website upon completion of review. JSPS aims for fair selection of review committee members using the database; committees are drawn from active researchers and previous grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of review results and content
rubrics_metrics.description: For some categories (e.g., Specially Promoted, Scientific Research S/A, Challenging Research Pioneering with Comprehensive Review) approximate ranking, opinions expressed in the review results, and other items will be disclosed; for categories using Two-Stage Document Review (e.g., Scientific Research B/C, Early-Career, Challenging Research Exploratory) the approximate ranking, review results by rating elements, the standard-format opinion, and other items will be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check category-specific disclosure practices on MEXT/JSPS websites for details on what will be published when not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and fairness of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS audits document and panel reviews to verify fairness (e.g., whether favors were dispensed or reviews conducted not in accordance with review rules). Findings of improper behavior affect future reviewer selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that review processes are monitored and JSPS will take action if impropriety is found (including changing reviewer selections in subsequent years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review methods (Two-Stage Document Review and Comprehensive Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-Stage Document Review is used for some categories (example: Scientific Research B/C, Challenging Research Exploratory, Early-Career) with multiple reviewers per proposal (example counts: B:6 reviewers, C/Early-Career:4, Challenging Exploratory:6–8). Comprehensive Review (example: Scientific Research A, Challenging Research Pioneering) includes both document review and multi-faceted panel review with typically 6–8 reviewers and may use preliminary screening or random assignment when many applications are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know which review method applies to your category; categories like S may use additional specialized reviewers. Changes to review methods (e.g., Challenging Research Exploratory switched to two-stage from FY2022) are possible—check current call documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of review section (Review Section Table)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants select the review section for their proposal from the Review Section Table; revisions to the table (e.g., changes to examples of related research content, joint reviews for some Basic Sections under Scientific Research (B)) can change where proposals are reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the latest Review Section Table (MEXT/JSPS websites) to choose the most appropriate section; joint reviews may consolidate sections with few applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of grant use and provisional grant decision
rubrics_metrics.description: KAKENHI funding can be used without interruption after the date of notice of provisional grant decision in the initial fiscal year until the end of the final fiscal year. New projects typically start April 1 (except some categories) and continued projects start April 1; Multi-year Fund projects can be used during the research period beyond fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After notice of provisional grant decision, necessary contracts (purchasing, hiring Research Collaborators) may be concluded and research started even before funds are disbursed. Note distinction between Notice of Review Results and Notice of Provisional Grant Decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbursement timing and institutional payment practice
rubrics_metrics.description: First-term disbursement to research institutions is remitted around July and second term around October; for Multi-year Fund second fiscal year onward the first term is at the fiscal year's beginning. Research institutions should pay or reimburse necessary expenses according to their accounting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your research institution for details on payment timing and whether temporary payments/reimbursements are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning unused funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an unused amount at the end of the research project period, it should be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returning unused amounts will not disadvantage subsequent KAKENHI reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management by research institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions carry out management and procedures for KAKENHI to reduce researcher burden and prevent inadvertent rule violations. Researchers must observe Supplementary Conditions, Funding Conditions, and institutional accounting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the person in charge at your institution for purchasing, delivery inspection, payment timing, and other management questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct expense permitted uses and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expense may be used broadly for expenses necessary to carry out the research project (purchase of goods, travel, personnel costs/honoraria, miscellaneous expenses), including expenses for compiling research results. Items not recognized as direct expense: costs for buildings/facilities (except installation costs necessary to install purchased goods), costs for handling accidents or disasters during implementation, personnel costs/honoraria for the PI or Co-Investigators, and other costs that should be covered by indirect expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI and Co-Investigators are obliged to be accountable for spending judgments. Consider social acceptability and appropriate priority when using direct expense; follow Spending Rules and institutional regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining direct expense with other funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expenses may be used in combination with other funds without restrictions on use, and combining direct expenses with other non-KAKENHI expenses that have restrictions is acceptable provided expenditure demarcation can be identified objectively (e.g., itinerary, purchased quantities, efforts). Combining different KAKENHI funds' direct expenses is acceptable subject to identifying expenditure demarcation and, under certain conditions starting FY2020, identifying cost burden and basis for calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document clear demarcation (percentages, quantities, project periods) and consult institutional managers; see MEXT guidance on combined purchases of joint-use facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared facilities and joint-use equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities purchased for a project may be shared among multiple research projects; combining funds (including different KAKENHI funds) can be used to purchase shared facilities as long as use does not interfere with the purchasing project's research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure use policies and cost allocation are established and consult your research institution before combining funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect expense rate and permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect expense is delivered to the research institution at a fixed ratio to direct expense: the amount equivalent to 30% of the direct expense will be provided as indirect expense. Institutions may use indirect expense to improve R&D environment and institutional research functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of allowable uses: personnel costs (including for PI/Co-Is), technical personnel for maintenance of shared equipment, facility maintenance, equipment costs, library/journal subscriptions, article publication charges, consumables for shared devices, research publicity, management costs for competitive funding, patent fees, and attorney fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications to research plan without prior application
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on research progress, certain changes can be made without applying or notifying JSPS: changing allocation of direct expense within a range of 50% of the total direct expense (or up to 3 million yen if 50% is ≤3 million), changes to division of roles, allocation shares to researchers, research schedule, breakdown of major goods, and partial changes within original research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions should be made appropriately to achieve original objectives and carry out research effectively; keep records and follow institutional procedures for internal approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major changes requiring application/notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Major changes—such as allocation changes in direct expense exceeding 50% of the total (or >3 million yen threshold)—require going through appropriate procedures in advance with JSPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning significant reallocation or scope changes, consult the Funding Conditions/Supplementary Conditions and submit required forms per JSPS guidance before executing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics, education, and integrity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs and Co-Investigators are expected to participate in research ethics and compliance education; participation status is confirmed at formal application for grant delivery and payment requests. Researchers must adhere to codes such as the Science Council of Japan's 'Code of Conduct for Scientists' and JSPS's 'For the Sound Development of Science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete institutional or JSPS-provided ethics training (e.g., Green Book, e-Learning Course on Research Ethics [eLCoRE]). Be proactive about disclosure, accountability, and societal impact evaluation of research; follow institutional rules on conflicts of interest and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory compliance depending on research content
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on research content, necessary procedures and compliance with laws/guidelines are required (examples include ethical guidelines for human subjects, acts/guidelines on human cloning/specified embryos, iPS cell guidance, gene therapy clinical trial guidelines, laws on living modified organisms, infectious disease acts, animal experiment guidelines, export controls, access to genetic resources, and personal information protection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify applicable laws/guidelines early and follow institutional review boards, biosafety committees, export control checks, and other mandated procedures; consult institutional offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for not following rules (penalties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improper grant spending, fraudulent grant acquisition, and research misconduct can lead to penalties: return of funds (partial or entire), suspension of eligibility to apply (ranges: 1–10 years for improper spending; 5 years for fraudulent acquisition; 1–10 years for research misconduct), suspension of funding for adopted projects, and public disclosure of fraud details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalties can affect collaborators and institutional administrators involved. Applications to other competitive funds may also be limited. Maintain research ethics and accurate accounting to avoid serious sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buyout system (direct expense covering non-research duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expense may cover costs of 'buyout'—hiring someone to take over duties other than research so the PI/Co-I can devote more time to research—starting from FY2021 for specified research categories (list provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants wishing to use the buyout system must follow the buyout scheme agreed between the applicant and their research institution and ensure their category is eligible (categories include Specially Promoted, Transformative Areas, Scientific Research, Challenging Research, Early-Career, Research Activity Start-up, certain international research categories, Special Purposes, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access expectation for KAKENHI-supported papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers supported by KAKENHI are, as a principle, to be handled under an open access policy established by JSPS. Exceptions allowed when open access is difficult due to copyright or institutional repository limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow JSPS Implementation Policy on Open Access and consider APCs (which can be handled via indirect expenses by the institution) and institutional repository options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher information registration and dissemination (researchmap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active registration of researcher information and research achievements on 'researchmap' is requested; researchmap is linked to e-Rad and institutional databases to enable open dissemination of research results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register and update research achievements to comply with JSPS requests and to facilitate public dissemination and government utilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-round schedule and planning (call/deadlines/review timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedules for calls and review result notices are provided (FY2023 examples): start of call, application deadlines, and timing of notice of review results vary by category (e.g., Transformative Areas May–July; Scientific Research categories early July–October). Reviews of new proposals are conducted earlier so notice of review results can be sent before provisional grant decision; Grant-in-Aid for Research Activity Start-up follows different schedule (call starts March 1; deadline mid-May).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan staffing, procurement, and travel based on expected notice and provisional grant decision dates; necessary contracts should be signed after provisional grant decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and transparency of review committees and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of review, names of review committee members are disclosed; JSPS discloses review policies and criteria via MEXT/JSPS websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult published review policies and criteria to align proposals with evaluation expectations; review committee composition and policies are public information after review.
